meta.title: Nossa Senhora das Graças de Cimbres — Cronologia
meta.subtitle: Chronology of the reported Marian apparitions at Cimbres, Pesqueira, Brazil (1936–present)
meta.description: An open, source-referenced chronology of the reported 1936 apparitions of Nossa Senhora das Graças at Cimbres (Pesqueira, Pernambuco, Brazil), the Church's response to them, and the shrine that grew at the site.
meta.dataQualityNote: Work-in-progress dataset compiled from public sources (see references). The apparitions are recorded here as REPORTED events: the dataset documents who reported what and when, and what Church authorities ruled and when — it does not assert the supernatural claim as fact. Sourcing for this subject is thin: much of the literature is devotional, and several dates rest on a single devotional source; those are flagged with a ? mark. Contested claims are attributed to their authors. Corrections against primary sources are welcome.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: A series of Marian apparitions reported in 1936 (and, per some accounts, into 1937) by two adolescent girls at Sítio Guarda, near the village of Cimbres, municipality of Pesqueira, Pernambuco, Brazil, attributed by the devotion to Nossa Senhora das Graças (Our Lady of Grace).

facts.label: Reported seers
facts.value: Maria da Conceição Silva (1920–1999), then 16, and Maria da Luz Teixeira de Carvalho (1922–2013), then 13 — the latter later a religious sister under the name Irmã Adélia.

facts.label: Church status
facts.value: No formal diocesan ruling from the 1930s–40s has been located: a 2023 academic study concludes the devotion consolidated 'without major institutional interference from the local Curia or the Roman Curia', while devotional literature reports informal dismissal and imposed silence. The first official pronouncement came on 2 October 2021, when Bishop José Luiz Ferreira Salles of Pesqueira published a pastoral letter recognizing the 'presumíveis aparições' (presumed apparitions), stating they show 'great probability of supernatural character', and permitting the devotion. This is a diocesan act, not a papal one.

facts.label: The site today
facts.value: A diocesan shrine — the Santuário de Nossa Senhora das Graças at Aldeia Guarda, Vila de Cimbres — with an annual pilgrimage feast on 31 August. The village and shrine lie inside the demarcated Xukuru Indigenous Land on the Serra do Ororubá.

approvalLadder.note: Each rung is a separate judgment by a separate authority, about a separate object; this page records what each one did and when, citing the act, and never adds them up into a verdict. For Cimbres the central finding is an absence: no formal diocesan ruling from the 1930s–40s has been located. The two documented recent acts are about different objects — the bishop's 2021 recognition of “presumíveis aparições” (presumed apparitions), and the beatification cause of one of the seers, which judges a person and not the events of 1936.

stages.label: Local inquiry — the investigators on the ground
stages.who: Fr. José Kehrle (1891–1978), secretary to the Bishop of Pesqueira, and Frei Estevam Roettger OFM (1877–1955), both acting on Bishop Adalberto Accioli Sobral's determination.
stages.outcome: The two investigators interrogated the seers repeatedly from August 1936 and attended the reported apparitions in person, pressing for a contradiction; the diocese's own 2021 pastoral letter records that they returned “o parecer favorável sobre os eventos e o atestado da sua veracidade” — a favourable opinion on the events and an attestation of their truthfulness. Kehrle's 1941 “Manuscripto” is that opinion, and it remains the principal source for every later account. It is an investigator's report and not a ruling: it was never published, Kehrle kept silent under obedience, and no diocesan act adopted it. The clergy were not of one mind — Msgr. Elyseu Duarte Diniz, questioning the girls separately on 31 August 1936, declared he believed none of it.

stages.label: The bishop's ruling, 1930s–40s
stages.when: 1936–1947 (the episcopate of Dom Adalberto Accioli Sobral)
stages.who: Bishop Adalberto Accioli Sobral (1887–1951), second bishop of Pesqueira, who administered the diocese from 1934 to 1947 and who ordered the inquiry.
stages.outcome: Devotional literature reports that the Church answered in this period by rejecting the reports and imposing silence — the Heralds of the Gospel add police pressure and some fifty years of enforced silence on the seers and on Kehrle — but it produces no decree, and that characterization is its own. What better sources establish is narrower and is not a ruling: the 2023 academic study finds the cult was legitimated by its devotees “without major institutional interference from the local Curia or the Roman Curia” and describes strategies of silencing rather than an act, while the diocese's 2021 pastoral letter records “silenciamento das autoridades eclesiásticas” and the detention of Maria da Luz's father by police in 1936, then calls itself “a primeira resposta da Igreja” — the Church's first response to these events. So a ruling is reported and no document has been located. That is not the same as a ruling against, and this page does not record one.
stages.noDocument: No formal diocesan decree on the apparitions, favourable or adverse, has been located for the 1930s–40s. Searched, August 2026: the 2023 RBHR study, which works from Kehrle's 1941 manuscript and cites no such act; the 2021 pastoral letter, which reviews the whole history and cites none either; Catholic press; the shrine's own history; and the devotional literature that asserts the rejection. The diocesan archive of Pesqueira — which holds Kehrle's manuscript, and where such a decree would be — is not online and has not been consulted. That archive is where this question gets settled.

stages.label: The bishop's judgment, 2021 — the pastoral letter
stages.who: Bishop José Luiz Ferreira Salles CSsR of Pesqueira, signing at Aldeia Guarda, Vila de Cimbres.
stages.outcome: The letter is titled “A Diocese de Pesqueira e as presumíveis aparições de Nossa Senhora da Graça” — presumed apparitions — and the word does work all through it. Acting “pela autoridade que nos confere o nosso ministério episcopal”, the bishop declares that in the reported apparitions there are “elementos, traços e sinais que abalizam e sinalizam a grande probabilidade do caráter sobrenatural” of what the two girls lived; that the messages are “em profunda consonância com as verdades da fé cristã”; that this finding of great probability, while making the events worthy of credence, “não vincula ou obriga nenhum fiel a crer”; and that he grants permission for the faithful to continue the devotion. Official interpretation is reserved to the Magisterium and to the diocesan bishop, and the letter says expressly that it does not exhaust the possibility of later decisions by the competent ecclesial authorities. It is a diocesan act finding a high probability and permitting a cult — not a declaration that the apparitions are established, and not a papal act.

stages.label: Referral to Rome on the apparitions
stages.who: The Holy See. The 2021 pastoral letter proceeds under the Holy See's 1978 norms for discerning presumed apparitions and reserves official pronouncements on the case to the Magisterium and to the diocesan bishop of Pesqueira.
stages.noDocument: Nothing found indicates that the apparitions were ever referred to Rome or ruled on there. Searched, August 2026: the 2023 RBHR study, which concludes the cult consolidated “without major institutional interference from the local Curia or the Roman Curia”; the 2021 pastoral letter, which reviews the case at length, cites the Roman norms, reports no Roman act on it and calls itself the Church's first response; Catholic press, which presents the 2021 act as diocesan; and the Latin title variants for a curial document, logged as a verified zero in this project's KEYWORDS.md. This is recorded as “no record found” — a statement about the evidence reached — and deliberately not as “the case did not reach this step”, which would be a claim about the case itself. Settling that would take the registers of the competent dicastery, which this project has not seen; a study's finding of no interference is compatible with a Roman act that did not interfere.

stages.label: Rome — the beatification cause of Irmã Adélia, a different object
stages.when: Nihil obstat 22–23 February 2024; diocesan phase 10 March – 13 October 2024
stages.who: The Dicastery for the Causes of Saints, and the Diocese of Pesqueira for the diocesan phase.
stages.outcome: This rung is about a person, not about the 1936 events. The Dicastery's nihil obstat opened the beatification and canonization cause of Irmã Adélia — Maria da Luz Teixeira de Carvalho, the younger of the two seers — which gives her the title Servant of God; Catholic press differs over whether the act fell on 22 or 23 February 2024. The diocesan phase opened on 10 March 2024 and closed on 13 October 2024, and the acts went to Rome, where the cause is under way. A cause examines a candidate's life and virtue: nothing in it is a judgment on the apparitions, and headlines of the form “the Vatican recognizes the apparition of Cimbres” misreport it. The 2021 pastoral letter had already announced that the nihil obstat was requested and awaited, treating the cause as a matter distinct from the events. The rung is here because it is the only Roman act in this file, and omitting it would leave that confusion unanswered.

events.title: The episcopal see is transferred to Pesqueira
events.text: The Diocese of Floresta (created 1910) is transferred to Pesqueira, taking in the parishes of Pesqueira and Cimbres among others; the Diocese of Pesqueira is the ecclesiastical authority over all later events in this chronology.

events.title: First reported apparition
events.text: Maria da Conceição Silva (16) and Maria da Luz Teixeira de Carvalho (13) report seeing a woman with a child on a rock of the Serra do Ororubá while gathering castor beans; in later reported dialogues the figure, asked who she was, answers 'Eu sou a graça' ('I am the grace'). Pilgrims begin arriving the next day, per the shrine's account.

events.title: The Diocese of Pesqueira opens an inquiry
events.text: After the reports reach the diocese, Bishop Adalberto Accioli Sobral designates his secretary, Fr. José Kehrle, to investigate the events and draft an opinion (parecer) on the credibility of the accounts, following canonical procedure. Devotional transcriptions date Kehrle's first recorded interrogation of Maria da Luz to 15 August 1936.

events.title: Mass gathering at the site; clergy divided
events.text: On a date the seers said the apparition itself had appointed, a crowd — over 5,000 pilgrims, per the shrine's account — gathers at the site; Kehrle's diary records the message 'Brazil is saved, communism is not coming any more'. The same day Msgr. Elyseu Duarte Diniz, after questioning the girls separately, declares he believes none of it, an early sign of the split Kehrle's diary describes among clergy and faithful.

events.title: Maria da Luz enters religious life
events.text: Maria da Luz enters the Damas da Instrução Cristã (Religious of Christian Instruction), taking the name Irmã Adélia; the December 1940 date rests on a devotional source, while Catholic press gives her perpetual profession as 1946. Her fellow seer Maria da Conceição remains a laywoman, and the academic literature notes her later 'silencing' — her subsequent life is thinly documented.

events.title: Kehrle's favorable report is completed — and no ruling follows
events.text: Fr. José Kehrle completes his 'Manuscripto', a diary-report concluding favorably on the reported apparitions; it becomes the principal source for later study. No formal diocesan judgment is documented: the 2023 academic study of the case concludes the cult was legitimated by devotees 'without major institutional interference from the local Curia or the Roman Curia', and describes strategies of silencing by the hierarchy — Kehrle kept his opinion unpublished under obedience. Devotional literature (Heralds of the Gospel) goes further, reporting a campaign of suppression that included police pressure and roughly fifty years of imposed silence on the seers and on Kehrle; that characterization is theirs.

events.title: An image of Nossa Senhora das Graças is enthroned in the chapel
events.text: Per the shrine's own history, an image of Nossa Senhora das Graças donated by Odete Berardo is enthroned in the small chapel that Arthur Teixeira de Carvalho, Maria da Luz's father, had built near the site. Single devotional source; date unverified elsewhere.

events.title: Irmã Adélia speaks publicly; large pilgrimages begin
events.text: Diagnosed with cancer described as terminal, Irmã Adélia breaks decades of silence and gives public testimony about the 1936 events; Catholic press reports that subsequent examinations found the cancer gone — a claim recorded here as reported, not verified. From this point organized pilgrimages of hundreds begin arriving, the first from Fortaleza, per the shrine's account.

events.title: The site is decreed a sanctuary
events.text: Per the shrine's own history, Bishop Manoel Palmeira da Rocha of Pesqueira decrees the site the Santuário de Nossa Senhora das Graças. The date rests on the shrine's account alone; the decree text has not been reached.

events.title: The Xukuru Indigenous Land, which contains Cimbres, is homologated
events.text: The Brazilian presidency homologates the demarcation of the 27,555-hectare Terra Indígena Xukuru on the Serra do Ororubá (decree published 2 May 2001). Vila de Cimbres and the sanctuary lie within this territory — the shrine's later history unfolds on demarcated Xukuru land, whose people also keep an older Marian devotion of their own, 'Mãe Tamain' (Nossa Senhora das Montanhas).

events.title: Pastoral letter recognizes the 'presumed apparitions'
events.text: Bishop José Luiz Ferreira Salles of Pesqueira signs, at Aldeia Guarda, a pastoral letter on the 'presumíveis aparições de Nossa Senhora da Graça': it states the reported events show 'elements, traces and signs that signal the great probability of the supernatural character' of the experience, finds the messages 'in deep consonance with the truths of the Christian faith', permits the devotion, and reserves interpretation of the events to the Church's magisterium and the diocesan bishop. Catholic press describes it as the Church's first official declaration on the case in 85 years.

events.title: Nihil obstat for Irmã Adélia's cause; she becomes 'Serva de Deus'
events.text: The Dicastery for the Causes of Saints grants the nihil obstat for opening the beatification cause of Irmã Adélia (Maria da Luz), who thereby receives the title Servant of God. Sources differ on the exact day — 22 February (feast of the Chair of St Peter, per Canção Nova) or 23 February 2024 (per other Catholic press). The act concerns the seer's cause, not the apparitions themselves.

events.title: Diocesan phase of Irmã Adélia's cause closes
events.text: The diocesan phase of the beatification and canonization process of Irmã Adélia, opened on 10 March 2024, is closed on 13 October 2024 — the eleventh anniversary of her death — and the acts are sent to Rome, per Catholic press.

figures.name: Irmã Adélia (Maria da Luz Teixeira de Carvalho)
figures.role: Reported seer, aged 13 in 1936; later a sister of the Religious of Christian Instruction; gave public testimony from 1985; declared Servant of God in 2024

figures.name: Maria da Conceição Silva
figures.role: Reported seer, aged 16 in 1936; remained a laywoman; the academic literature notes her later 'silencing' and her life is thinly documented

figures.name: Fr. José Kehrle
figures.role: German-born secretary of the Diocese of Pesqueira; conducted the 1936 diocesan inquiry and authored the favorable 'Manuscripto' (1941), the principal source on the events

figures.name: Dom Adalberto Accioli Sobral
figures.role: Bishop of Pesqueira 1934–1947; ordered the inquiry. Devotional literature reports he personally dismissed the case; the academic study records no formal ruling by him either way

figures.name: Frei Estevão von Roettger, OFM
figures.role: Franciscan who conducted complementary questioning of the seers; devotional and Catholic-press accounts report his diary attested to the events' authenticity

figures.name: Dom José Luiz Ferreira Salles, CSsR
figures.role: Bishop of Pesqueira; author of the 2 October 2021 pastoral letter recognizing the 'presumed apparitions' and petitioner for Irmã Adélia's cause

organizations.name: Diocese of Pesqueira
organizations.founded: 1910 (as Diocese of Floresta; see transferred to Pesqueira 1918)
organizations.relation: The competent ecclesiastical authority over the reported apparitions and the shrine: it ran the 1936 inquiry, issued no documented ruling for decades, and published the 2021 pastoral letter.

organizations.name: Santuário de Nossa Senhora das Graças (Cimbres)
organizations.founded: 1998 (decree reported by the shrine; chapel from the late 1930s–1940s)
organizations.place: Aldeia Guarda, Vila de Cimbres, Pesqueira, Brazil
organizations.relation: The diocesan shrine at the reported apparition site, attached to the parish of Nossa Senhora das Montanhas; destination of the annual 31 August pilgrimage feast.

organizations.name: Povo Xukuru do Ororubá
organizations.founded: Indigenous people of the Serra do Ororubá; territory homologated 2001
organizations.relation: The indigenous people on whose demarcated land Vila de Cimbres and the sanctuary stand. They are the territorial context of this chronology, not a party to the apparition claim; they keep an older Marian devotion of their own ('Mãe Tamain' / Nossa Senhora das Montanhas). Their wider history — including the land struggle — is documented elsewhere and is not this project's subject.

organizations.name: Religious of Christian Instruction (Damas da Instrução Cristã)
organizations.founded: 1817, Ghent (Belgium); in Brazil from the 19th–20th century
organizations.relation: The congregation Maria da Luz entered (as Irmã Adélia) around December 1940; it announced her recognition as Servant of God in 2024.

disambiguation.note: An obscure, mostly devotional literature surrounds this subject; the distinctions below are the ones most often flattened in it.

items.title: Cimbres 1936 ≠ the Miraculous Medal (Paris, 1830)
items.text: 'Nossa Senhora das Graças' is also the Brazilian title of Our Lady of Graces of the Miraculous Medal (Rue du Bac, Paris, 1830). The Cimbres devotion uses the same title — per the inquiry records because the reported figure answered 'Eu sou a graça' — but it is a distinct reported apparition with its own history.

items.title: The 2021 'recognition' is diocesan, not a Vatican approval of the apparitions
items.text: The 2 October 2021 act is a pastoral letter of the Bishop of Pesqueira on 'presumed apparitions' asserting 'great probability' of supernatural character. The 2024 Vatican act (the Dicastery for the Causes of Saints' nihil obstat) concerns Irmã Adélia's beatification cause, not the apparitions — despite press headlines such as 'Vatican recognizes apparition'.

items.title: Documented silence ≠ a published condemnation
items.text: Devotional tradition speaks of early Church rejection of Cimbres. What the sources actually show is narrower: no formal decree — negative or positive — has been located for the 1930s–40s; the academic study documents informal dismissal, non-publication of Kehrle's favorable report, and strategies of silencing, and devotional literature adds (on its own authority) police pressure and decades of imposed silence. This dataset records that absence rather than inventing a ruling.

items.title: Mãe Tamain ≠ Nossa Senhora das Graças de Cimbres
items.text: The Xukuru devotion to Nossa Senhora das Montanhas, called 'Mãe Tamain', predates 1936 and is the patroness of the local parish; it is distinct from the 1936 apparition devotion, though both share the same mountain.
